simple.meaning: עֶצֶר (ʻetser) is a Hebrew word meaning “restraint.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֶצֶר (H6114) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֶצֶר (H6114) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֶצֶר (ʻetser) / H6114 is traced through Judges 18:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then the five men departed and came to Laish and saw the people who were there, how they lived in safety, in the way of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; for there was no one in the land possessing authority, that might put them to shame in anything, and they were far from the Sidonians, and had no dealings with anyone else.

definitions.full: H6114. etser עֶ֫צֶר noun [masculine] restraint (?), only ע ׳יוֺרֵשׁ Judg 18:7 a possessor of restraint , i.e. ruler, but ᵑ9 ᵐ5 wealth , so Thes and others, text very dubious, compare GFM Bu conjecture that ׳ע combines readings אֹצָר and עשֶׁר .
